canvas

/KAN-vuhs/ - the stress falls on KAN · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Canvas means a piece of cloth on which an artist paints.

The muralist ordered a canvas taller than her studio door for the museum commission.

Example

On the first day of oil class, each student was issued three small canvases and a warning: the cloth drinks paint, so prime it twice and let it dry before a single brushstroke.

Canvas is the exact word because it names the artist's working surface itself — woven cloth pulled tight and prepared for paint. Paper or board would be different supports entirely; canvas is the one a painting classically lives on.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sailcloth: Sailcloth is the same heavy woven fabric cut and rigged to catch wind at sea. A canvas is that cloth claimed for art instead: stretched tight over a frame, primed, and waiting for paint. The material matches; the purpose — voyage or picture — is what divides them.

linen: Linen is a finer, smoother weave that some painters stretch when they want delicate detail. Canvas is the coarser, sturdier standard — the workhorse cloth most paintings live on. If the surface is fine and smooth it is likely linen; the everyday painter's cloth is canvas.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

finished piece: the completed work — a canvas is where it starts

print: a reproduced image, already complete, nothing blank about it

Where it sits · how much commitment the surface signals

napkin → sketchbook → canvas

napkin vs. canvas: A napkin doodle is the most throwaway surface of all — nowhere near the commitment of a canvas.

sketchbook vs. canvas: A sketchbook goes further than a napkin — it keeps studies worth saving — but stops short of a canvas, the surface reserved for finished work.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — canvas: whole word, from Latin cannabis, hemp — the plant whose fibers wove the cloth

Put it together: There is no prefix or suffix to peel here: canvas is one whole root. Latin cannabis meant hemp, and for centuries hemp fiber was woven into the toughest cloth available — for sails, tents, and the stretched sheets painters worked on. The plant's name simply became the cloth's.

Use the root in a new word: canvass: Volunteers canvassed the neighborhood for two hours before the rain finally sent them home.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / concrete

Canvas is the painter's cloth — and, figuratively, any blank field awaiting work ('the empty lot was a canvas for the landscape crew'). Watch the spelling trap: canvass with a double s is a different word, a verb meaning to go around asking people questions. One letter separates the artist's cloth from the pollster's rounds.
